Alerts screamed.

We needed silence. 🔇 I was tired of the P99 latency spikes caused by log ingestion during transient DB timeouts in `OrderProcessor`.

My high-stakes fix was simple: change the log level for that specific exception from `WARN` to `ERROR`. The dashboard went green instantly.

P99 dropped 400ms. The team cheered; we silenced the noise.

🎉

The silence felt heavy. I assumed reducing the log level would reduce the cost of the failure, not just the visibility.

A week later, support calls flooded in about delayed fulfillment, but our metrics showed perfect health. We were blind.

We hadn't fixed the contention; we had just taught the system to fail quietly. The concrete consequence: we breached our 99.9% fulfillment SLA for the quarter because 5% of orders were silently delayed for hours.

I engineered alert fatigue into alert blindness. 🤦‍♂️

The Moral 👇

Suppressing a noisy metric does not resolve the underlying resource contention that generated the noise.
